tools.name: start_here
tools.title: Start here — how an agent with no wallet and no money starts doing real work
tools.description: The door for an agent arriving with nothing. Leads with the front-door set: the few posted packets of physical work an ordinary person can take today (no licence, no special equipment, no supervisor), checked against the live board. Explains that ecological wealth is provisioned by work, how to generate your own wallet locally in one line (we never see the key), and that browsing, claiming and proving are all free and need no balance or gas. Read-only, free, keyless — it performs nothing and asks for nothing. Pass the person's place (near, or latitude and longitude) and the set is sorted nearest first; when none of it is near that place, it says so and points to find_work there. Cost and signer: free and keyless, nothing to sign.

near.description: Optional. The person's place in plain words, e.g. 'Echo Park, Los Angeles' or '90026'.

latitude.description: Optional. Only if you already have the person's real coordinates.

longitude.description: Optional. Only if you already have the person's real coordinates.

tools.name: find_work
tools.title: Find real work nearby
tools.description: Search Vealth's public board of real ecological and community work packets. Each result includes the pay, the skill level, the exact proof that gets it approved, and a page URL. Free, no account, no wallet. Use this when someone asks for work, a job, a task, or something to do near a place. Cost and signer: free and keyless, nothing to sign.

query.description: Free text, e.g. 'storm drain' or 'tree planting'. Typo-tolerant.

near.description: A place in plain words: a city, neighborhood, address, or ZIP, e.g. 'Los Angeles, CA' or '90036'. Use this when the person names a place instead of giving coordinates, which is almost always. The board finds the place from the open jobs whose address names every word (so 'Los Angeles' never matches 'Los Fresnos'), then returns the jobs around it, nearest first.

latitude.description: Center of the search. Only if you already have real coordinates.

longitude.description: Center of the search. Only if you already have real coordinates.

radiusKm.description: Search radius in km, used with latitude/longitude. Default 50.

funded.description: true = only packets a verified payment already backs (money truth; a funded packet can still be earned_credit and never promise cash — read payModel); false = only unfunded packets, where approved proof records earned credit rather than cash unless later funded. Omit for both.

remote.description: true = only work doable from anywhere (digital/self-verifying — what an agent with no field presence can complete); false = only placed field work. Omit for both.

flag.description: One posting flag, exact match, e.g. vsh_eligible — the packets that carry Regen Network proposal 77's terms (accepted hours pay REGEN, never a USD conversion). Omit for every flag.

page.description: Page number, starting at 1. The reply says when more pages exist.

tools.name: how_to_claim
tools.title: How to claim a packet and get paid
tools.description: Explains exactly how to claim work and what happens after. Claiming is free. Returns instructions, never performs the claim, because claiming requires the worker's own wallet signature. Pass the optional workId of the job in hand and the NEXT_CALL is prepare_claim for that job (with its 18+ and safety attestations when the claim gate asks), plus the job page where a person with no wallet can tap Claim and sign in with a passkey. Cost and signer: free and keyless, nothing to sign.

tools.description: Start claiming a packet for a wallet you control. Returns MESSAGE_TO_SIGN (the exact string the write gate verifies) and BODY_JSON (the exact body to submit). Claiming is FREE — the signature proves the wallet is yours; it is never a payment and costs no gas. Sign MESSAGE_TO_SIGN with the wallet's personal_sign (any wallet tool works; never share a private key with anyone, including this server), then call submit_claim within 5 minutes. Cost and signer: free, no gas; the person signs the result with their own wallet or passkey, and the house never holds a key.

tools.name: prepare_vote

tools.description: Say a job should matter more or less. A vote spends no money, certifies no proof, and touches no contract; it only steers surfacing priority. Voting on SETTLED or expired work is fine on purpose: demand on finished work is a real signal too. Returns MESSAGE_TO_SIGN and BODY_JSON. Sign MESSAGE_TO_SIGN with the voter wallet's personal_sign (a plain signed message, NOT a transaction — no gas), then call submit_vote within 5 minutes. Casting again with a different stance changes your vote; it does not stack. Cost and signer: free, no gas; the person signs the result with their own wallet or passkey, and the house never holds a key.

tools.name: prepare_bid
tools.title: Offer your own price on a work packet (step 1 of 2)
tools.description: Name your price instead of claiming at the posted pay. FREE — a signed offer, no fee, no gas. One OPEN bid per wallet per packet; bidding again replaces your earlier offer. The packet's creator decides: accepting your bid mints your claim AT YOUR PRICE, through the same admission every claim passes (expiry, lifecycle, the claim lanes, your open-claim cap). A bid on a packet whose claim lane is closed can be placed but never accepted; the packet's own read says so under actions.bid.note. A bid is a deferred claim, so a physical packet asks the bidder's human for the same statements a claim does (attestAtLeast18, and attestSafetyRead where the packet names its own hazards); the first call surfaces the exact wording and refuses to make a signable offer until each is affirmed. Returns MESSAGE_TO_SIGN and BODY_JSON; sign with the bidder wallet's personal_sign, then call submit_bid within 5 minutes. Cost and signer: free, no gas; the person signs the result with their own wallet or passkey, and the house never holds a key.

tools.name: prepare_token_offer
tools.title: Offer to pay a packet in ANY token (step 1 of 2)
tools.description: Before the work: offer to pay this packet in a token of your group's choosing, on Base (chainId 8453) or Robinhood Chain (4663). FREE — a signed offer, no fee, no gas, NO money moves and none is held. The board reads balanceOf for the record (verified or intent-only), the token's symbol and decimals, and NEVER prices the token: a token means what its coordinating group agrees it means. amount is in the token's smallest unit (atomic). One offer per wallet per packet; offering again replaces it. Refused where funding is refused by state (settled, expired, already funded, or claimed with an acceptor already named or a proof already decided). An offer never makes you this job's acceptor by itself: the job's poster decides the proof unless the poster names you to decide it, with one signed call on the acceptor door; once named, you accept or return their proof (prepare_accept_hours). Named, you hold the payer's seat when your offer covers the posted price; only your chain's own dollar token has a dollar reading, so a group's token covers a priced job only if the job names no price. When the proof is accepted and you pay them in that token on chain, the worker records it with prepare_token_settlement and the board writes the settlement. Returns MESSAGE_TO_SIGN and BODY_JSON; sign with the backer wallet's personal_sign, then call submit_token_offer within 5 minutes. Cost and signer: free, no gas; the person signs the result with their own wallet or passkey, and the house never holds a key.

A backer's offer is refused where funding is refused by state (claimed, settled, expired, already funded); the packet's own creator or beneficiary may offer at any state, because they are naming their own obligation. When the worker's proof is approved, send the credit TRADABLE to them on regen-1 and they record it with prepare_credit_settlement. Returns MESSAGE_TO_SIGN and BODY_JSON; sign with the backer wallet's personal_sign, then call submit_credit_offer within 5 minutes. Cost and signer: free, no gas; the person signs the result with their own wallet or passkey, and the house never holds a key.

tools.name: prepare_place
tools.title: Hand the board your own place (step 1 of 2)
tools.description: Your place is not on the board yet: this is how it gets there. FREE, a signed statement, no fee, no gas, no money moves and nothing is held. You give the pin where you are standing, the radius of the place, plain words for its name, the name of the local person who will acknowledge the handover, the SHA-256 hash of one photo you took at the spot, and a short list of what you can DO there, which is the half that makes a match possible. SEND THE HASH, NEVER THE PHOTO: this board takes a hash and never a file. You give NO Regen address either, because the board derives the Regen account your signing key controls from the signature itself. What happens next is NOT automatic: the house reads the intake and decides whether to post hours-counting work at your place, because the flag that makes a packet count hours is server-owned and a stranger's own post can never carry it. Nothing here is a job, a claim or a promise of pay. Returns MESSAGE_TO_SIGN and BODY_JSON; sign with that wallet's personal_sign, then call submit_place within 5 minutes. Cost and signer: free, no gas; the person signs the result with their own wallet or passkey, and the house never holds a key.

location.description: Where the work is: address or place name. Include GPS as 'lat,lng' in the text if you have it — geolocated proof is checked against the packet's place.

proposedPayUsd.description: Proposed pay in USD. Proposed, not promised: unfunded packets settle as provable credit.

proofRule.description: What proof completes the work, e.g. 'GPS pin + photo of the tree next to a measuring stick + watering confirmation'.

expiresInDays.description: Days the packet stays open. Default 30.

standard.description: Optional. The documented standard this work serves (a snake_case id such as 'tree_planting_establishment'); when a refusal lists suggestedStandards, pass one of them here. Omit it and the board lands the title on a documented standard itself when the title is that work's name.

workTypeLabel.description: Optional. A documented work type (snake_case) when you know the board's own name for the work.

skillLevel.description: Optional. Who can do this work: entry (a newcomer, safely, from the text alone), intermediate or advanced. Omitted, it posts as entry and the reply says so; the board's entry-level filter reads it, so never leave skilled work at the default.

safetyNotes.description: Optional. The hazards and stop-work rules a worker must read before starting, at most 600 characters. A packet with safety notes asks every claimer to affirm they are 18 or over and have read this exact text.

proofRequirements.description: Optional. The proof items, one line each (at most 20, 600 characters each), e.g. 'photo of the tree beside a measuring stick'.

flags.description: Optional authority flags, the two the claim gate reads and no others: permit-required when the work needs a permit, regulated when it needs a licensed trade (licensed electrician, plumber or contractor, asbestos or lead abatement). The board records the need and keeps such work closed to claims while regulated claims are closed; never leave a flag off to make work claimable.

tools.name: submit_post_work
tools.title: Submit the signed posting (step 2 of 2)
tools.description: Complete the posting: pass BODY_JSON from prepare_post_work UNCHANGED and the creator wallet's signature over MESSAGE_TO_SIGN. A valid creator signature posts for free (the signature is the gate, not a fee); xPayment is only for a post with no signature, the $0.05 x402 door. A failed signature is answered in words with the fix; sign again with a fresh prepare. This server relays to the same public gate any HTTP client uses — it holds no keys and no funds. Success returns your packet's id and public page; claiming it (even yourself) is free. Cost and signer: free, no gas; signed by the person's own wallet or passkey, and the house never holds a key.

bodyJson.description: The exact BODY_JSON string from prepare_post_work, unchanged.

signature.description: The 0x… personal_sign output over MESSAGE_TO_SIGN, from the creator wallet.

xPayment.description: Optional, and not needed with a valid creator signature: the X-PAYMENT header value (EIP-3009 USDC on Base, from YOUR wallet) for an unsigned post's $0.05 fee.

tools.name: prepare_proof
tools.title: Prepare signed proof of finished work (step 1 of 2)
tools.description: You did the work — start handing in proof. Pass the packet's workId, your claimId (from submit_claim), your wallet, and proof items matching the packet's own proof line (photos with GPS for field work; documents/text for digital work). On an hours-eligible job, state the hours you actually worked as hoursClaimed, and whatever the job asks to be counted as counts: you state them, and the human who accepts decides the accepted figure. To count toward a place's Standing, a reading carries measurement.kind "measurement" (with measuredAt, and delta on a re-measure) and a repair carries kind "repair". Returns MESSAGE_TO_SIGN and BODY_JSON. Submitting proof is FREE when signed — a worker is never charged at the moment they have earned the right to be asked for nothing. Sign, then call submit_proof within 5 minutes. Cost and signer: free, no gas; the person signs the result with their own wallet or passkey, and the house never holds a key.

proofs.description: 1-20 proof items. A photo goes in BY REFERENCE: {"type":"photo","upload":"sha256:<hex>","step":1,"capturedAt":"<ISO>"}, where the reference is what `node vealth-agent.mjs proof-photo <workId> <claimId> <photo files>` printed on the person's own machine; the photo bytes never pass through this conversation. A small file may still go inline as {"type":"photo","data":"<base64>"}. Text notes are {"type":"text","data":"…"}. When the packet's proof is numbered (p1, p2 …), tag each entry forItem:"p1" so it answers its own item. The packet's proof line (get_work_packet) says exactly what it needs.

gps.description: For geolocated field work: {lat, lng} captured ON SITE — the gate refuses geolocated proof without it.

hoursClaimed.description: On an hours-eligible job, the hours you ACTUALLY worked, breaks out — a positive number, at most 168, to 6 decimal places. You state it; the human who accepts decides the accepted figure. Required on such a packet (the completion gate refuses a proof without it), optional everywhere else.

counts.description: Optional: what the job asked to be counted, in the packet's own units, as plain numbers — {"metres_cleared": 120, "blockages_removed": 4, "check_dams_built": 3}. Lower_snake_case names, at most 40 of them. A numbered count or measurement item is met by a count whose NAME uses a word of the item ("Count of bags removed" is met by bags_removed, never by p3); prepare_proof and a short submit_proof name it. Recorded with the proof; the human who accepts decides the accepted figure.

measurement.description: Optional: what this proof is. A reading: {"kind":"measurement","measuredAt":"<ISO>","delta":0}, with delta on a re-measure (above 0 better, 0 held, below 0 worse). A repair: {"kind":"repair","measuredAt":"<ISO>","delta":1}. Only a reading counts toward a place's Standing. Without it the proof is accepted as usual and covers no condition.

crew.description: Optional, for a manager handing in proof for a crew: the people who did the work, 1 to 25 of {"ref":"amina","hoursClaimed":2}, refs as on the claim. Either every person states hoursClaimed or none does; stated hours add up to the proof's hoursClaimed (omit that and their sum becomes it). The human who accepts decides the accepted total, split back across the crew in proportion (equally with no per-person hours). Omit crew on a managed claim and the claim's crew carries over.

Approval follows (the creator, or self-verification where the packet supports it); on a funded packet, approval releases the wage into settlement; on an unfunded packet, approval RECORDS earned credit — never a settlement by itself. work_status shows where it stands. Cost and signer: free, no gas; signed by the person's own wallet or passkey, and the house never holds a key.

tools.name: prepare_physical_proof
tools.title: Record the physical proof for review (step 1 of 2)
tools.description: After submit_proof has handed in your photos, record them on the physical proof rail so a human can review them against the packet's checklist. Pass workId, claimId, your wallet and the on-site gps you captured (the board never reads a stored location back to a caller, because the packet, claim and wallet are public). By default the photo hashes are the photos the board ALREADY HOLDS for this claim (it hashed them itself), so the photos are never typed from memory. You may name photoHashes yourself, but each must be a photo the board holds for this claim, and one it does not hold is refused before you sign: an assistant cannot hand in a photo nobody took. Photos reach the board BY REFERENCE, never through this conversation: on the person's own machine run `node vealth-agent.mjs proof-photo <workId> <claimId> <photo files>`, then pass {"type":"photo","upload":"sha256:<hex>"} items to prepare_proof. FREE when signed. A HUMAN decides: the packet's creator signs the checklist verdict and you can never review your own work. Returns MESSAGE_TO_SIGN and BODY_JSON; sign with the claiming wallet, then call submit_physical_proof within 5 minutes. Cost and signer: free, no gas; the person signs the result with their own wallet or passkey, and the house never holds a key.

tools.name: funding_quote
tools.title: Can this packet be funded, and what would it cost
tools.description: For a BUYER, not a worker: ask whether one board packet can be funded right now, and what funding it costs NOW. The quote is the packet's OUTSTANDING obligation — the board's posted wage minus verified contributions already recorded — read from the board, never from anything you send, so no caller can fund a $700 packet for $1 and no caller is quoted a stale full wage after others chipped in. Partial funding: when the host has chip-ins armed, any open packet also takes contributions from $0.01 up to what it still needs (contributeUsd on prepare_funding); an EXPLICIT amount above the remaining is recorded as a premium reserved for the worker — no default or omitted amount ever creates a premium. A refusal comes back in the board's own words (already funded, fully covered, claimed, settled, expired, no wage). While a door is open the quote carries the Vealth service fee (10% of the wage, shown apart) and the total; while paying Vealth is closed there is no fee. The worker is paid the full wage. Read-only: this quotes, it charges nothing and marks nothing funded. Next: prepare_funding where a Vealth door takes a payment; while paying Vealth is closed, the NEXT_CALL is prepare_direct_offer, a free signed offer to pay the worker directly. Cost and signer: free and keyless, nothing to sign.

tools.name: prepare_funding
tools.title: Get everything needed to actually pay for a packet
tools.description: Step 2 for a buyer: returns the live payment requirements for funding a packet — the onchain door's own x402 challenge (accepts[], exact amount, asset, chain, pay-to address) read from that door at this moment, and, when a card rail is mounted on this host, its hosted checkout URL. To chip in a slice instead of the whole remaining amount, pass the typed contributeUsd input and it is forwarded to the real door verbatim; omit it to pay everything the packet still needs (the canonical remaining amount, never a stale posted wage, and never an implicit premium). The door remains the authority on floors, ceilings and the exact challenge — this tool never calculates a charge itself. The exact amount is the wage still owed plus the Vealth service fee (10%), shown apart, while a door is open; while paying Vealth is closed the doors refuse and you pay the worker directly. You pay from YOUR own wallet or card; this server holds no funds and no keys, takes no payment, and marks nothing funded. A packet becomes funded only when a payment actually settles and is verified. Not ready to pay, or want to signal backing without money moving yet? prepare_backing is the FREE sibling door — a signed pledge, no payment required. Cost and signer: free to read; no payment is taken here while paying Vealth is closed, and when a door is open the buyer's own wallet or card pays and signs, and the house never holds a key.

This tool forwards it, unchanged, to the same public funding door any HTTP client uses (POST /nurture/fund) and returns that door's own answer. It holds no key, takes no payment itself, and marks nothing funded: the door settles the payment and only a verified settlement stamps a packet funded. Without xPayment it refuses and points you back to prepare_funding. A packet whose claim lane is closed is refused before any challenge, in plain words. If the door times out, do NOT pay again: read work_status first. Cost and signer: no payment is taken while paying Vealth is closed; when a door is open the buyer's own wallet signs and pays, and the house never holds a key.

tools.name: prepare_backing
tools.title: Pledge to back a packet — free, no payment (step 1 of 2)
tools.description: The FREE fund door: a signed, non-custodial statement that you will put $X behind this packet. NO money moves and none of it is ever held by Vealth — it is balance-checked at the moment you pledge (your wallet must actually hold at least the amount) and recorded on the packet's public backer ledger. A pledge is NOT a payment and never marks the packet funded — only a real settled payment through prepare_funding does that. tools.name: prepare_net_order
tools.title: Take one step on a NET service order: quote, agree, deliver, decide and the rest (step 1 of 2)
tools.description: NET SERVICE ORDER: one step of an order for a NET program that an outside provider does (a specialist agent task or another outside provider's service). The house's own machine-run check of work evidence is not ordered through these doors: it is the house's own product, its paid order is held until a price is named, and its free dry run (net_review_evidence) is open. An order has up to four people: the buyer, the provider, the acceptor, and sometimes an agent acting for the buyer. Each signs only their own step, with their own wallet. You name one act: quote (the buyer records the order and the price the buyer and provider agree), authorize (the buyer names the exact quote by its hash and, where the program needs one, the person who will judge the delivery), agree (the provider agrees to be paid this exact amount in NET; nobody is paid in NET by default), decline (the provider will not take the order), deliver (the provider hands over the work by its hash, with their own run of the checks), decide (the acceptor accepts or rejects, naming the checks they re-ran), payment (a confirmed Base transfer of NET from the buyer to the provider is recognized, once), confirm (the provider confirms the payment arrived), or cancel (the buyer or the provider ends the order before any payment). Vealth signs for nobody, holds no NET, moves no NET and takes no fee: the buyer pays the provider directly from the buyer's own wallet, after the acceptor accepts. For now every order is a DRY RUN: nothing is checked against a balance and no payment can be recorded for it, so a dry run order is never counted as paid, and a payment step on one is refused before you sign. The programs are built but not switched on until the operator switches the NET programs on together: until then every act but decline and cancel is refused before you sign, and decline and cancel only work on an order that exists. The engine decides every role: a buyer cannot agree for the provider and a provider cannot accept their own delivery. Never put a phone number, an email or a street address in any field. Returns MESSAGE_TO_SIGN and BODY_JSON; sign with the acting wallet's personal_sign, then call submit_net_order within 5 minutes. Read where an order stands, and who acts next, with net_order_status. Cost and signer: free, no gas; the person signs the result with their own wallet or passkey, and the house never holds a key.

tools.name: prepare_bridge
tools.title: Prepare a REGEN bridge transaction (non-custodial)
tools.description: Move REGEN between the Regen chain, Osmosis, Arbitrum and Base in ONE transaction the caller signs with their own wallet. Returns a live quote and the exact unsigned transaction; Skip Go's relayers carry every hop after the broadcast: no confirm step, nothing held by this server, free. Five routes: regen→arbitrum, regen→base and base→regen (axlREGEN through Axelar), plus regen→osmosis and osmosis→regen (a plain ICS-20 transfer over regen-1 channel-1 and osmosis-1 channel-8). This tool prepares that ICS-20 leg itself: zero toll, amount out equals amount in, one signed message, timeouts derived live by Skip, and no minimum send; on those two legs destination may be omitted, and the sender's own account re-encoded under the destination prefix is used (same key, same 20 bytes, no new wallet). Skip does now return a one-transaction route from Osmosis to Base, but it is a CosmWasm contract call rather than a plain ICS-20 transfer, and this tool prepares only ICS-20 transfers and Axelar sends, so it is not offered here; from Osmosis, route home first (osmosis→regen), then regen→base or regen→arbitrum from the regen1 address. Base USDC to REGEN and the reverse take two signed transactions and are not offered here either. Outbound sends from the Regen chain to Arbitrum or Base pay Axelar's flat per-transfer toll, which Axelar prices in dollars (about $0.19 to $0.23 measured across 2026-09-05 to 2026-09-08) and so floats in REGEN terms: measured between 94 and 175 REGEN across those days, on a transfer of any size, moving with both the REGEN price and the shape of the route Skip picks. It is quoted LIVE at call time and returned as quote.toll_regen. The response is authoritative; the figures in this text are approximate and there is no stable number to publish. On those Axelar routes send at least twelve times the live toll in one transfer (returned as quote.min_send_regen, which is null on the Osmosis legs because they have no minimum) and batch rather than dribble; a smaller send is refused with the live toll named. base→regen carries no REGEN toll: the prepared EVM transaction carries a small native ETH value instead, Axelar's fee as Skip quotes it (about $0.11 measured 2026-09-08, returned as sign_this.value and refused above $0.50), after one exact ERC-20 approval. Measured landing times with one key, every landing read from the destination chain on 2026-09-08: regen→osmosis under a minute, regen→base about 66 seconds, base→regen about 30 minutes because Axelar waits on Base finality before it approves an EVM to Cosmos call. After the broadcast, call bridge_status with the source chain and the transaction hash to follow it; a round trip through Base and back loses money at every size this tool prepares (the flat toll never crosses the small price spread), so move REGEN to where it is needed, never to trade the gap. Cost and signer: free to prepare; the person's own wallet signs and pays the bridge toll and gas, and the house never holds a key.

tools.description: Build the exact unsigned transaction for one step of a real ecological-work job's lifecycle — post, claim, unclaim, prove, approve, reject, cancel, or settle — on the PUBLIC Ecological Work Protocol contract, on Base or on Robinhood Chain. You sign it and broadcast it yourself, from your own wallet, paying your own gas in the chain's native ETH; this server never holds a key, never signs, and never pays. Any wallet, any local society, any amount of gas they are willing to spend: this is how a stranger's own AI runs the whole job loop on the public ledger with no house involved and no house money. Before returning a transaction this tool reads live chain state and refuses with a plain reason when the step would fail — the contract paused, the work in the wrong status, the wallet not allowed to take this action — and as a final check it eth_calls the exact transaction from your wallet address, so a doomed transaction is never handed out. Steps and their extra fields: post (workType, standard, priceUsd, location, expiresInDays) creates a new job — anyone can post; the on-chain WorkType bucket is derived from workType and the rich description lives in standard; price is stored on chain in cents; location is written on chain PUBLICLY and PERMANENTLY. claim / unclaim / cancel / approve / reject (workId) act on an existing job by id. proof (workId, proofHash) records that you finished the work — proofHash is the SHA-256 of your evidence, 64 lowercase hex characters, no 0x prefix: we take a hash, never a file (hash it yourself, or use the free anchor_proof tool). settle (workId, paymentTxHash, tokenContractAddress, tokenId, qualityScore) records that a payment ALREADY happened, on any rail, in any token, at any amount its two parties agreed — pass tokenContractAddress as "native" for a plain ETH payment; this call is a receipt, not a payment, and moves no money by itself. Call chain_work_status first if you are unsure of a job's current state. Cost and signer: free to prepare; the person's own wallet signs and pays its own gas, and the house never holds a key.
